# Selvedge — full reference for AI agents

> Long-term memory for AI-coded codebases. A `git blame` for AI agents — but for the *why*, not just which line which model touched. Captured live, by the agent, as the change happens. Local MCP server, SQLite storage, zero dependencies, MIT. `pip install selvedge`.

This file is a single self-contained reference an AI agent can ingest to understand what Selvedge is, when to use it, and how to call it.

## What it is

Selvedge is a local Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) call it as they work to log structured change events with reasoning, and to read prior reasoning before they act. The data stays in a SQLite file under `.selvedge/` next to the code. No cloud, no external dependencies.

The problem it solves: human-written code leaks intent everywhere — commit messages, PR descriptions, inline comments, the chat that preceded it. AI-written code doesn't. The agent has perfect clarity about *why* it made each decision, but that context lives in the prompt and evaporates when the conversation ends. Six months later `git blame` tells you *what* changed and *when* — it can't tell you *why*. Selvedge captures the why, live, by the agent itself, as the change is made.

Why "captured live" matters: tools like AgentDiff and Origin generate reasoning *after* the change by feeding the diff back to a second LLM. Selvedge's reasoning is the agent's own intent, written from the same context window that produced the change — no inference, no hallucinated explanations, and an empty `reasoning` field is itself a useful signal.

Why "entity-level" matters: most tools attribute *lines*. Selvedge attributes the things you actually search for — `users.email`, `env/STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `api/v1/checkout`, `deps/stripe`. The first question after `git blame` is usually "what's the history of this column", not "what's the history of lines 40–48".

The store is append-only, and since v0.3.11 it is tamper-evident: every logged event gets a SHA-256 chain record written in the same transaction, and `selvedge verify` recomputes the chain end to end (`chain_intact` fails hard on any row edited, deleted, or reordered out-of-band; `chain_coverage` warns — never fails — about rows that predate the chain on upgraded installs). Honest scope: this detects casual and accidental modification; it is not proof against a motivated local attacker, who controls the file and can recompute every digest.

## Install and setup

```
pip install selvedge
cd your-project
selvedge setup
```

`selvedge setup` is an interactive wizard: it detects which AI tools you have (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot), writes the MCP entry into each one's config, drops the canonical agent-instructions block into your prompt file (`CLAUDE.md` / `.cursorrules` / `copilot-instructions.md`), runs `selvedge init`, and installs the post-commit hook. Every modified file gets a `.bak` first. Re-running is a no-op.

Claude Code plugin (alternative): `/plugin marketplace add masondelan/selvedge` then `/plugin install selvedge@selvedge` (run `pip install selvedge` first).

## The 8 MCP tools

- `log_change` — record a change event with entity, diff, and reasoning. Pass `rename_from` with `change_type="rename"` for the dual-event rename pattern. `change_type="reject"` (v0.3.11) records "considered and decided against" without writing the change; `expires_when` attaches a machine-checkable expiry condition (`library:NAME>=VERSION`, `entity:PATH:changes`, `date:ISO`, `manual:LABEL` — validated at write time).
- `diff` — history for an entity or entity prefix.
- `blame` — most recent change + context for an exact entity.
- `history` — filtered history across all entities.
- `changeset` — all events grouped under a named feature/task slug.
- `search` — full-text search across all events.
- `prior_attempts` — prior change attempts on an entity + outcome (was it tried and reverted, or considered and rejected?). Call it before editing. An attempt closed by an explicit `revert`/`reject` event reports `confidence: "exact"` (v0.3.11 — the outcome is stated in the log, not inferred); the add→remove proximity heuristic is the tiebreaker for implicit removals. Conservative by design: `min_confidence` defaults to `proximity_high`, `exact` rows always clear that floor, and an empty list is a trustworthy "nothing to worry about".
- `stale_decisions` — decisions due for a revisit: `expired` (a machine-checkable `expires_when` condition fired — evaluated locally from installed packages, the event log, and the clock; `manual_review` when a `library:` dependency isn't locally observable), `revisit_due` (past `revisit_after` *and* still in active use — pure age never surfaces), or `review_suggested` (a later change matched the decision's `stale_when`).

## Entity-path conventions

```
users.email           DB column (table.column)
users                 DB table
src/auth.py::login    Function in a file (path::symbol)
src/auth.py           File
api/v1/users          API route
deps/stripe           Dependency
env/STRIPE_SECRET_KEY Environment variable
```

Prefix queries work everywhere: `users` returns `users`, `users.email`, `users.created_at`, etc.

## The canonical agent-instructions block

This is what `selvedge setup` / `selvedge prompt` installs into your project's `CLAUDE.md` / `.cursorrules`. It is the single source of truth for when an agent should call Selvedge:

```
## Selvedge — change tracking

You have access to Selvedge (MCP server: `selvedge`) for change tracking.

Rules:
- Call `selvedge.log_change` immediately after adding, modifying, or removing any DB column, table, function, API endpoint, dependency, or env variable.
- Set `reasoning` to the user's original request or the problem being solved. Write at least one full sentence.
- Set `agent` to the tool you're using, e.g. "claude-code", "cursor", or "codex".
- Set `git_commit` to the commit hash once you know it.
- For multi-entity changes, set a shared `changeset_id` on all related calls (a short slug like `add-stripe-billing`).
- Before editing an entity, call `selvedge.prior_attempts` on it — if the same change was tried before and reverted, you'll see the prior reasoning and why it was rejected, and can change your plan instead of repeating a rejected approach.
- A reverted decision is not a permanent ban. If the constraint that killed it no longer holds, re-open it explicitly with `change_type="supersede"` (never re-apply a reverted change without superseding it first).
- Log abandoned paths too: use `change_type="reject"` when you considered an approach and decided against it without writing it, and `change_type="revert"` when you rolled a change back — ideally with `stale_when` or `expires_when` naming the condition that would invalidate the verdict.
- Then call `selvedge.diff` or `selvedge.blame` for the entity's broader history before conflicting with past decisions.

The same operations are on your shell: `selvedge prior-attempts <entity>`, `selvedge blame <entity>`, `selvedge log <entity> <change_type> --reasoning "<why>"`, `selvedge supersede <entity> --reasoning "<why>"`, `selvedge search "<query>"`, `selvedge history --since 7d`, `selvedge stale`. Add `--json` to any read command.
```

## Stopping repeated reverted mistakes (prior_attempts)

The failure mode: an agent re-tries a change a previous session already made and reverted, because the reason for the revert lived in a chat session that's gone. The code went back; the why didn't go anywhere the next agent can read. The fix: before editing an entity, the agent calls `prior_attempts` on it — one tool call, before anything is written.

Worked example (full case study: https://selvedge.sh/prior-attempts — transcript: https://github.com/masondelan/selvedge/blob/main/docs/demos/prior-attempts.md). An agent asked to keep mobile users signed in across restarts is about to re-add a `users.auth_token` column that an earlier session added and reverted:

```jsonc
// tool call
prior_attempts({ "entity_path": "users.auth_token" })

// tool result  (default min_confidence = "proximity_high")
[
  {
    "entity_path": "users.auth_token",
    "change_type": "add",
    "timestamp": "2026-03-12T17:40:11Z",
    "reasoning": "Store a per-user auth token so the mobile app can stay signed in across restarts.",
    "outcome": "reverted",
    "confidence": "proximity_high",
    "outcome_reasoning": "Reverted: tokens in the DB meant we couldn't revoke without a write; moved to short-lived JWTs verified statelessly. Column unused."
  }
]
```

The agent reads why the change was rejected (DB-stored tokens couldn't be revoked without a write; the team standardized on short-lived stateless JWTs), keeps the JWT approach, and solves the problem compatibly — a refresh token in the OS keychain plus a stateless `/auth/refresh` endpoint — then logs its own reasoning with `log_change` so the next session inherits the decision.

Facts:

- `prior_attempts` is a deterministic SQLite query with templated output. No LLM, no API key, no network — which is why an empty result is a trustworthy "nothing to worry about" rather than noise.
- Default `min_confidence="proximity_high"` returns the high-signal rows: stated outcomes (`confidence: "exact"` — the attempt was closed by an explicit `revert` or `reject`, or the row is a standalone rejection; v0.3.11) plus the clear tried-then-reverted proximity cases. Pass `min_confidence="proximity_low"` to widen recall to the speculative tail. If you filter on `confidence`, accept `exact` wherever you accepted `proximity_high`.
- Each hit is the full change event (`entity_path`, `change_type`, `timestamp`, `reasoning` — why the change was made — plus the rest of the event record) with always-present outcome fields on top: `outcome` (`reverted` / `rejected` / `reopened` / `active`), `confidence`, `outcome_reasoning` (why it was reverted or rejected), and the supersede-trail fields. Every field always populated, never null.
- History from before Selvedge was installed isn't there — backfill with `selvedge import` (reads SQL DDL, Alembic migrations, and Agent Trace records); coverage grows from the day it's installed.

## How Selvedge compares

| | Reasoning source | Granularity | Mechanism | Grouping | Storage |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Selvedge | Captured live, by the agent in the same context that produced the change | Entity (column, table, env var, dep, route, function) | MCP server — agent calls it as work happens | Changesets across many entities | SQLite, zero deps |
| OpenLore | Derived — tree-sitter static analysis of code state, plus commit-gated decision notes | AST node (18 languages + 12 IaC) | MCP server — one-time index + commit-time certificates | Call-graph edges | SQLite graph in `.openlore/` |
| AgentDiff (sunilmallya) | Inferred post-hoc by Claude Haiku from the diff at session end | Line | Claude Code lifecycle hooks → local daemon | Session/task | JSONL on disk |
| Origin | Prompt receipts, captured live per turn | Line | Agent lifecycle hooks + git post-commit hook | None | Git notes + sessions branch |
| Git AI | Attribution metadata | Line | Agent-invoked checkpoint → Git notes at commit | None | Git notes |
| BlamePrompt | Prompt receipts — prompt, cost, tools; no stated rationale | Line | Agent-lifecycle hooks + post-commit hook | None | Git notes |

Selvedge does not replace git (line-level what/when), PR review tools, or agent observability (LLM call traces). It sits between them — the provenance-as-first-class-citizen layer.

## Picking a codebase-memory MCP server

"Codebase memory" is four different jobs wearing one name. Pick by the memory you're missing:

| Job | The question it answers | Representative servers |
|---|---|---|
| Code intelligence | "How is this codebase structured — who calls what?" | codebase-memory-mcp, OpenLore |
| Session context | "What was I doing before this session died?" | Memory Keeper (mcp-memory-keeper) |
| General memory | "What do we know about this user/project?" | mem0, official server-memory, claude-code-memory |
| Decision provenance | "Why is the code like this — and what was already tried?" | Selvedge |

Guidance:

- Pick codebase-memory-mcp for the strongest structure index (call tracing, dead code) — things Selvedge doesn't do at all.
- Pick OpenLore for a structure index plus decision notes from one deterministic local-first server — the closest thing to Selvedge in the category. The decisive difference: OpenLore derives memory from code state and purges rejected decisions from its queryable store after each sync (a decision synced before rejection leaves an annotation in the spec markdown; the queryable record is what disappears). Selvedge keeps rejected paths queryable.
- Pick Memory Keeper for resuming long sessions that die with un-checkpointed context.
- Pick mem0 or the official memory server for durable facts and preferences that follow a user across applications.
- Pick Selvedge when the question is "why is the code like this?" or "was this already tried?" — it's the only one where a rejected path stays queryable with reasoning attached, which is the record `prior_attempts` needs to stop an agent re-making a reverted mistake.
- These compose: Claude Code runs multiple MCP servers side by side, and a structure index plus a decision log beats either alone.

Selvedge memory also has a lifecycle: events can carry `revisit_after` dates, `stale_when` conditions, machine-checkable `expires_when` conditions (evaluated locally — no network, no LLM), and supersede links, so `stale_decisions` surfaces decisions that have expired or come due while still in active use, and a re-opened decision keeps its tried → reverted → re-opened chain instead of being rewritten.

Full page: https://selvedge.sh/compare/codebase-memory-mcp-servers/

## Agent Trace

[Agent Trace](https://agent-trace.dev/) is an open wire format for AI code attribution traces, published by Cursor (RFC, Jan 2026). Its original GitHub home went 404 in August 2026; the spec and schema survive, frozen at v0.1.0, at agent-trace.dev. Selvedge emits and reads that format — Agent Trace is the wire format; Selvedge is the live capture + query layer — with no runtime dependency on the upstream project.

```
selvedge export --format agent-trace    # emit Agent Trace v0.1.0 records (--ndjson, --collapse-by-session)
selvedge import --format agent-trace     # round-trip a Selvedge export, or ingest foreign producers best-effort
```

Selvedge's reasoning and entity-level provenance ride along in each record's `metadata` under the reverse-domain `dev.selvedge` namespace.
